dedupe_keys.name: global disaster data platform 全球灾害数据平台 gddat

description: The Global Disaster Data Platform (GDDAT) is a Chinese portal that publishes global disaster data in near real time, shares analysis and assessment products, and aims to support disaster risk management decisions. The portal read on 2026-09-28 offers real-time monitoring, feature analysis, a data retrieval search with advanced filters, a China disaster database and assessment products and data; its live summary for the twelve months to 28 September 2026 counted 1,508 events (677 earthquakes, 420 wildfires, 262 floods, 105 storms, 27 volcanic events, 17 droughts), about 400 million people affected and economic losses, with the countries most affected, led by China, Mozambique and Japan. Coverage is global with a national database for China, in Chinese and English. Access is free for guests, with login or registration for some functions; no licence is stated and the host institution is not named on the page. Caveats: loss figures and methods are not documented on the home page, some counts look inconsistent (losses in thousand dollars), and the site renders only with scripts. It supports hazard exposure and emergency response analysis from event records and cross-checks against other disaster databases. No related record is catalogued for this platform; EM-DAT-style event databases serve a similar purpose.
